newsitem.title: ITALY: International community pledges to help Albania.
newsitem.headline: International community pledges to help Albania.

text.p: The international community pledged on Thursday to help Albania rebuild itself, but warned Tirana it must restore public order, improve human rights and adopt sound economic policies.

"The international community stands ready to assist Albania," said a document drawn up by participants of a conference in Rome on how to reconstruct Albania's shattered economy, the poorest in Europe.

"Albanian parties must recognise the responsibility lies primarily in their own hands and that international assistance will depend on the degree of cooperation they provide...law and order must be restored in Albania and the respect of human rights and democratic standards enhanced," it said.

It also warned that "other conditions for effective donors' assistance are the adoption, in agreement with the IMF, of sound budgetary and monetary policies and in particular a viable budget for 1997".
The day-long meeting, attended by delegations from 35 countries and international organisations, will be followed by a larger donors' conference on Albania's future in the autumn.

"Within the international community there is one opinion, one view, one approach," said Franz Vranitsky, the mediator for Albania from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), at a news conference.
"We will continue to fill the framework with substance with regard to the reconstruction of the Albanian police force, of the army, of commerce, of financial systems and of the constitution."

Vranitsky said the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank would send teams to Tirana in August to help with economic programmes, including setting up banking systems and advising on how to deal effectively with pyramid schemes.

The collapse of shaky investment schemes earlier this year swallowed the life savings of tens of thousands of Albanians and triggered months of anarchy which led to the fall of the government of former President Sali Berisha.

Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini confirmed Italy would leave a residual military force in Albania after a 7,000-strong multinational security force currently deployed there completes its withdrawal on August 12.
Italian officials have said the new force will be entrusted with civil duties including helping train Albanian military and police forces.
Fatos Nano, the new Albanian Prime Minister who triumphed in a recent general election, attended the conference and pronounced himself pleased with the results.
"Our (government) programme has not only received a (parliamentary) vote of confidence but today it has received a vote of confidence from the international community," he said.
